canonical_statement: The study sought to determine whether a BSA-guided initial heparin bolus or a fixed 10,000-U bolus was more effective at producing desired initial arterial ACT values of 350 or 400 seconds during PTCA.
Patients who had received heparin before PTCA were not included.

canonical_statement: The study compared 27 patients receiving BSA-adjusted heparin with 27 age- and gender-matched controls receiving the traditional 10,000-U bolus.

canonical_statement: The desired procedural arterial ACT target was defined as greater than 400 seconds; a 350-second threshold was also evaluated because lower ACT targets were used at other institutions.

outcome.definition: Arterial ACT >400 s; ACT >350 s also evaluated

canonical_statement: Arterial ACT was measured using a Hemochron Model 401 blood coagulation timing system.
For ACT measurement, 2 mL of blood was drawn from the femoral arterial vascular sheath after a 3-mL discard, and the line was flushed with normal saline without heparin.
ACT was measured at baseline before the procedure and again 10 minutes after the initial heparin bolus.

Numerical data were expressed as mean +/- SD; a paired Student t test was used for between-group BSA and ACT comparisons, a z test for proportions compared target-attainment rates, tests were two-tailed, and p<0.05 was considered significant.
A central pharmacodynamic outcome was arterial ACT 10 minutes after the initial heparin bolus.
Target attainment was evaluated as the proportion of patients with a 10-minute arterial ACT greater than 400 seconds and, separately, greater than 350 seconds.
Mean BSA was 1.92 +/- 0.18 m^2 in the BSA-guided group and 1.87 +/- 0.24 m^2 in controls, with no significant difference between groups.

canonical_statement: The BSA dosing formula was derived empirically after observing that a 10,000-U bolus in patients with BSA around 1.3 m^2 produced an ACT around 400 seconds in several patients.
Under the empirical formula, a patient with BSA 1.7 m^2 would receive an initial heparin bolus of approximately 13,000 U.

canonical_statement: Venous ACT values tend to be slightly greater than arterial ACT values, so target-attainment percentages would be somewhat different if venous sampling were used.
At ACT values above 300 seconds, Hemochron values tend to run at least 50 seconds higher than HemoTec values, so ACT targets are not directly interchangeable between devices.
The heparin-dose formula was empirical and depended on the assumption that heparin requirements generally follow body size.
The authors cited biological plausibility for size-adjusted dosing: variation in patient size requires variation in heparin dose to obtain the desired anticoagulant effect.
BSA adjustment of the initial heparin dose before PTCA was more effective than a fixed 10,000-U bolus for reaching arterial Hemochron ACT targets of 350 and 400 seconds.
